docs.title: Welcome to PAMPAS
docs.text:
This documentation refers to the driverless system of the Brazilian FSAE electrical team Ampera Racing of the Federal University of Santa Catarina.

PAMPAS stands for Prototype AMP Autonomous Driving System. The AMP part refers to the name of our electrical protoype, which in turn comes from Ampera, the name of the team. The Pampas are also a grasslands ecoregion that covers part of sourthen Brazil.

docs.title: First steps
docs.text:
This page is dedicated for new members of the Ampera Electrical FSAE team that are part of the Driverless subteam.

Here you're going to find the material you should study during your training process. You don't need to master the contents linked here, but it's important you get a good grasp of the basics, and as such the resources here are at the introductory.

The sections are ordered in (my) recommended order of study and divided in weeks. Each

For the exercises, there is a base repository in our GitHub organization page that you can fork, clone and work on.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text: Complete the getting started nad Command line chapters of the Grasshopper section of the Linux Journey guide.

docs.title: Week 1: CS50
docs.text: Complete the first 6 weeks of the CS50 Hardvard introduction course to computer science. This course includes an intro to Python.

docs.title: Git
docs.text:
Chapters 1, 2 and 6 form the Pro Git book. Chapter 6 is also recommended.

From the Main level, at least the Introduction Sequence and Ramping Up sections; and from the Remote tab at least the Push & Pull -- Git Remotes! section from the Learn Git Branching guide.

docs.title: ROS
docs.text: Read the About ROS and complete the Get started section of the ROS 2 official documentation.
